title: A monthly retreat day
hookLine: a half day of quiet each month; Jesus tells his friends to come apart and rest a while, and the crowd gets there first
tomorrow: after the flood, God's first promise wasn't the rainbow. what was?

lines: NO LEISURE SO MUCH AS TO EAT.
COME APART AND REST A WHILE.
cards: The calendar is full, the phone keeps buzzing, and lunch happens standing up. Mark's Gospel describes a week like that.
Jesus has sent his twelve apostles out two by two, and now they're back, full of stories, and the crowd around them is so thick that, Mark says, "they had no leisure so much as to eat."
So Jesus says to them: "Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while." They get into a boat and push off.

teach.b: But people see them leaving. They run ahead on foot, out of all the towns, and get there first. When Jesus steps out of the boat, the quiet place is full.
And Mark says he "was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd."

He begins to teach them many things, and as the day wears on he feeds them, about five thousand men, with five loaves and two fishes. Christian teachers draw two things from this scene, and keep both.
First, withdrawal belongs to the life Jesus gave his friends: come apart, rest a while. Christian retreats, and the monthly days of recollection some keep, draw on lines like this one.
Second, the retreat isn't a wall. When real need meets you on the shore, compassion comes first, and the rest waits for another day.
A monthly retreat day holds both. Half a day, set apart, with the phone off and nothing to produce: a walk, a long sit, a notebook, a text you love.
And if someone you love truly needs you that morning, Mark's story doesn't treat that as a failed retreat. There it becomes compassion, and you go back for the rest next time.

how: Christians make retreats at retreat houses, monasteries or parishes, from a few hours to several days; some Catholics keep a monthly day of recollection, a few hours of quiet, prayer and reading.

games.q: what does “a monthly retreat day” mean?
o: half a day each month, set apart to rest
a week-long silent stay at a monastery
a monthly day off spent on errands

games.q: the rest that got interrupted: tap the pairs.
p: no leisure so much as to eat
where Jesus took them to rest
ran ahead and got there first

s: in the Gospels, Jesus never takes time away from the crowds
in Mark 6 he takes his friends apart to rest a while.
the crowd reached the quiet place before the boat did
they ran ahead on foot; the retreat was full when Jesus arrived.
Mark treats the interrupted rest as a failure
Mark says he was moved with compassion, and taught them.

games.q: your retreat morning is set: phone off, a walk, a notebook. at nine, your sister calls in tears. what fits Mark's story?
o: answer: in Mark, compassion came first and the rest waited.
ignore it: a retreat only works if nothing gets in.
answer, then give up on retreats; they never work.
games.why: Jesus called his friends apart to rest, and when the crowd beat them there, he was moved with compassion. the rest could wait.

practice: Close your eyes and picture a desert place of your own: a park bench, a library corner, a room with the door shut. See yourself there for half a day, with nothing to produce.
When you open your eyes, pick the date of your first one this month.

wordCard.voice: A monthly retreat day: half a day each month set apart to rest, the way Jesus called his friends to come apart.

orig.note: Greek, Mark 6:31: rest yourselves. The word inside come apart and rest a while.

carryVoice: The line for today: retreat day. Come apart and rest a while, and let compassion open the door if it knocks. See you soon.

sources.ref: Mark 6:7, 6:30–44 (the twelve sent two by two, their return, the crowd running ahead, the feeding of the five thousand)
